thread:
Lina (Finance): Heads up — pricing team ran the Q1 promo experiment and auto-applied retro credits for qualifying customers. Billing batch applied credits on 2025-03-31 which moved revenue recognition for several invoices. Need guidance on how to treat the retro credits for month-end JE. I pulled the list: customers impacted ~12, total credits = $62,430.
Omar (Billing Ops): Confirmed we pushed the credit adjustments as negative invoices (adj docs) in the March billing run. Those negative invoices reduced AR and revenue at posting. We have the audit file: /srv/billing/audit/mar_q1_promo_adjustments.csv
Tess (Product Pricing): The experiment rules granted credits for usage above a threshold in Jan-Feb. We authorized the credits to be applied retroactively to keep adoption experiments clean. We thought credits would be handled as marketing contra-revenue, not revenue deferrals.
Ivy (RevMgmt): Need to be careful. If the credits are effectively discounts applied to originally recognized revenue and customers had recognized product usage in Jan/Feb, then GAAP says reduce revenue in the period originally recognized or create a catch-up adjustment if immaterial. For month-end close we can't just drop revenue in Mar without documenting.
Lina (Finance): What's our proposed approach? Post a March adjustment reversing revenue and AR? Or record a deferral and amortize?
Omar (Billing Ops): Operationally easiest is to post negative invoices (already done). But finance needs the accounting treatment: either 1) restate Jan/Feb revenue (not ideal at close), 2) record March-period contra-revenue (affects current month), or 3) set up a marketing accrual to cover credits and leave revenue as originally recognized.
Tess (Product Pricing): Product prefers option 3 since this was an acquisition promotion and should hit marketing/COGS rather than core MRR impacts. Customers signed standard contracts.
Ivy (RevMgmt): Option 3 could work if credits are marketing spend (contra-expense) and we can justify they are not changes to customer consideration. Need tied documentation showing credits for adoption incentives and that they're not refunds for non-delivery.
Lina (Finance): For month-end close I need a recommended JE and owners. Also need a list of impacted invoice numbers and GL guidance.
Omar (Billing Ops): Attaching quick list in thread: INV-10021, INV-10057, INV-10433, INV-10789, INV-10901 (and 7 more). Total credit $62,430.
accounting-bot: Ticket created: ACCT-2025-3387. Please attach promo design doc and approval email.
Ivy (RevMgmt): Here's recommended treatment: record a Marketing Promotion Accrual (GL 6105) for $62,430 charged to Marketing Expense, credit Accounts Payable (or Accrued Liabilities GL 2105) in March. When credits are invoiced/posted, clear the accrual and apply the billing adjustments to AR. Memo: Q1 Promo retroactive credits — treat as marketing incentives per documented promo terms.
Tess (Product Pricing): That aligns with our intent. Well provide the experiment design doc and approval chain.
Lina (Finance): Draft JE as Ivy suggested: Date 2025-03-31 DR 6105 Marketing Promotion Expense $62,430 CR 2105 Accrued Promotions $62,430. Memo: Q1 promo retro credits; pre-funded accrual pending billing adjustments; attach experiment doc. Approvers? Need Finance Dir + CFO sign-off.
Omar (Billing Ops): Ill tag the audit CSV to ticket ACCT-2025-3387 and stop auto-posting any more retro credits until sign-off.
Ivy (RevMgmt): I'll route to Finance Dir for approval and add rev impact analysis: FYI if we had booked contra-revenue in March instead, net ARR delta would show -1.2% for the month.
Lina (Finance): Perfect. Putting JR-2025-1102 together and routing for approvals. Once approved we'll post accrual and clear when billing confirms negative invoices. Thanks team.
